name: create_trigger
description: Create a natural-language trigger for the current user. A trigger has three parts: an **if** condition (`trigger_nl_condition` — when to fire), a **fire message** (`trigger_fire_message` — what to deliver when it fires), and a **destination** (where to deliver — a destination id from `get_trigger_destinations`, defaulting to `event_log`). Only call this after the user has explicitly asked to create a trigger — do not create speculatively. If the user wants to send the fire somewhere specific, call `get_trigger_destinations` first to see the available ids.

scope_path.description: Wiki-relative path of the file or directory to watch. Use a `.md` path (e.g. `auth/passwords.md`) to watch one doc, or a directory path (e.g. `auth`) to watch every doc beneath it. Use `/` (or an empty string) to watch the whole wiki.

trigger_nl_condition.description: **If condition.** Plain-language description of when the trigger should fire (e.g. "when the auth flow's session-timeout policy changes"). Evaluated by an LLM against the diff, so be specific about what kind of change matters.

trigger_fire_message.description: **What message to send.** The notification body delivered when the trigger fires (e.g. "Auth: session timeout policy changed — please review"). Will appear in the destination.

destination.description: **Where to send it.** A destination id from `get_trigger_destinations` (e.g. `event_log`). Optional — defaults to `event_log`, which records the fire in the events table without sending it externally.
